notes: Identity verified independently from canonical text: title The Impact of the AIDS Pandemic on Health Services in Africa: Evidence from Demographic and Health Surveys; Anne Case & Christina Paxson; Demography (2011) 48:675–697; DOI 10.1007/s13524-011-0026-3. This is the primary published report, with article body, Tables 1–5, figures, and references; Online Resource 1 is referenced but not supplied. No PDF was named in the input. All assigned original fields examined together. study_o, description, locators_o, and es_type_o provide no target specification. No statistic is assigned by input order or numeric correspondence. Unselected printed candidates: Table 3 (p.685), outcomes had antenatal care / urine test / blood test / blood pressure / weight taken: observations 177,785 / 68,867 / 68,830 / 68,880 / 68,923; OLS HIV coefficients without country-region fixed effects 1.708 / –1.760 / –0.130 / –0.381 / 0.186; with fixed effects –1.734 / –2.220 / –1.214 / –2.058 / –1.403. Table 4 (p.687), clinic delivery / public clinic conditional on clinic delivery / trained birth attendant: observations 221,421 / 98,360 / 216,901; coefficients without fixed effects 1.013 / –1.156 / 0.541; with fixed effects –0.768 / –0.509 / –1.353. Table 5 (p.687), polio at birth / polio / measles / BCG / DPT: observations 157,395 / 212,266 / 211,582 / 212,361 / 212,260; coefficients without fixed effects –0.868 / 0.511 / 0.802 / 0.860 / 0.968; with fixed effects –7.018 / –2.708 / –2.767 / –2.021 / –2.657. These are printed OLS coefficients, not converted standardized effects. Tables give both ordinary and region-clustered standard errors, not a uniquely assigned p. Other candidate tests include Hausman tests (p.684 footnote 9), e.g. urine-test chi-square 3.58, p=.0668; polio chi-square 4.83, p=.0894; measles chi-square 2.04, p=.3602; semiparametric tests refer to Online Resource 1 Table 7 (p.689). These candidate values are not extracted target values. Analytic roles/exclusions: p.677 identifies birth-level samples, restricted to surviving mothers, and vaccination data generally for surviving children; footnote 4 excludes 133 missing maternal education cases and 3,509 missing region cases. P.684 describes trimming outcome-specific birth years without observations from at least four countries. The 14 countries and 119 regions are not substituted for analytic birth N. No N sum or effect conversion performed. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
